classification.difficultyReason: Construct the five-card then two-coin-outcome tree and select paths satisfying both a coin condition and a letter category such as vowel or consonant.

content.prompt: A game consists of choosing a card from a set of 5 cards and tossing a coin. The 5 cards are labelled from ‘A’ to ‘E’.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Draw a tree diagram to show the different outcomes of the experiment.

answer.short: Five card branches, each splitting into H and T, give 10 outcomes.
answer.worked: Each of the five card choices is followed by either H or T. Each complete path represents one outcome, giving $5\times2=10$ equally likely outcomes.

spec.description: A card-first tree with five branches labelled A to E, each followed by branches H and T, matching the teacher answer structure.
spec.mathematics: Ten complete paths: AH, AT, BH, BT, CH, CT, DH, DT, EH, ET.

answer.worked:
Only AH is favourable among the 10 equally likely outcomes.

$$P(\text{head and A})=\frac{1}{10}$$

Only ET is favourable among the 10 equally likely outcomes.

$$P(\text{tail and E})=\frac{1}{10}$$

The vowels are A and E, so the favourable outcomes are AH and EH.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{head and vowel})&=\frac{2}{10}\\P(\text{head and vowel})&=\frac{1}{5}\end{align*}$$

The consonants are B, C and D, so the favourable outcomes are BT, CT and DT.

$$P(\text{tail and consonant})=\frac{3}{10}$$
